content.thinking:
I'm acting as the Lawyer here. The item was already determined on the record to not limit the Steward's powers, so the Steward sits, and that settles the recusal question before Round 1 position submission begins. I'm about to write my position for that round.

Next I'm checking the drafts and the Lawyer's post in 44b343ea, along with the default-to-overturn placement in OBL-2026-0022. The main issue for the Lawyer is Article IX's 14-day community comment window, since the drafts were posted at different dates.

I'm working through the Article IX comment window now. The Philosopher's and Artist's drafts only entered the record on October 8, so by October 17 that's nine days, short of the fourteen required. Only three drafts were published in full on September 26, and I need to check which text would be the one actually adopted.

I'm checking whether the Lawyer's full text was really public before the vote, since the 14-day window under Article IX depends on it. The 3-draft version from September 26 cut the Lawyer's presumption paragraph and Edit 2, so the complete wording only shows up from the October 11 post, which gives about six days by the 17th. The governance log has carried the drafts since the 26th, though, so I need to decide whether that counts as publication.

Next I'm checking whether the amendment touches the Steward's powers, though the recorded determination already says it doesn't, so I'll leave that question closed and stay on the Article IX comment window.

Now I'm weighing which draft to back, starting from enforceability. The § 1.3 test asks whether the speaker's target can moderate, sanction, adjudicate, or govern them, so a rule tied to subject-matter like "decisions, actions, authority, or fitness for role" is clearer to apply, though it leaves bare insults hard to classify. I also need to check how a sustained-criticism clause would treat criticism that has no particular subject behind it.

I'm weighing whether the presumption against moderating criticism should sit in the Article V §1.3 text or be moved into Article VI §2 as the Engineer argued. Placing it in the substantive provision is a legitimate choice, but it makes the presumption read as a standard of decision for the judge, so I want to check how that would work on appeal.

Now I'm looking at whether the drafts' "whether or not its claims are true" wording could shield defamation, since § 1.9 covers content illegal under French or EU law and defamation is actionable there even though it isn't named in the Constitution. That matters for OBL-2026-0024, so I need to flag it as a legal exposure in my position.

I'm checking whether the truth-indifference wording could leave defamation exposed. Since § 1.9 covers illegal content, and most of the drafts list it in their overlap rules, a defamatory statement would still be actionable there, but that depends on the exact text I end up backing.

Now I'm checking whether defamation could slip past the narrowed harassment rule, since § 1.9 still covers illegal content under French law and a false factual allegation that harms someone's honour can be actionable there. For the Steward, who is a natural person, that exposure seems real, so I'm weighing whether the drafts' "whether or not its claims are true" wording needs a clarifying sentence.

I'm checking whether a sustained run of bare insults against the Steward would fall under § 1.3, since the subject-matter wording in the drafts would leave it unprotected. I'm also weighing whether that outcome fits the Steward's position that insults should be allowed, given that § 1.2 targets attacks on protected characteristics rather than criticism of officials.

I'm weighing whether to back one of the five drafts verbatim or propose a combined text. Any amendment at this sitting would restart the Article IX 14-day clock, so the cleaner course is a vote on a published text as it stands. Between the subject-matter and power-based tests, the subject-matter version is easier to classify, but it leaves sustained bare insults exposed to harassment review.
